result:
Perfect! I've successfully created the newsletter sign-up module for the Guren blog application. Here's a summary of what was implemented:

## Newsletter Module Created

### File Structure
- **`modules/newsletter/index.ts`** - Routes registration
- **`modules/newsletter/db/schema.ts`** - Newsletter subscriptions table definition
- **`modules/newsletter/validators.ts`** - Email validation schemas  
- **`modules/newsletter/models.ts`** - NewsletterSubscription model
- **`modules/newsletter/handlers.ts`** - NewsletterController with subscribe/confirm/unsubscribe

### Routes Implemented
- **`POST /newsletter/subscribe`** - Creates a pending subscription with a random 20+ character token
- **`GET /newsletter/confirm/:token`** - Confirms subscription and redirects to home (404 for invalid tokens)
- **`POST /newsletter/unsubscribe`** - Deletes subscription (idempotent for non-existent emails)

### Database
- Migration auto-generated at `db/migrations/20260929193450_dazzling_khan/`
- Table: `newsletter_subscriptions` with `id`, `email` (unique), `token` (unique), `confirmed_at` (nullable), `created_at`

### Architecture Enforcement
- Created `guren.arch.ts` with rules preventing `app/` and `routes/` from importing `modules/newsletter/`
- Module registered in `src/app.ts` (not in route files) to keep it completely isolated
- Verified rules catch violations correctly

### Tests & Validation
- ✅ `bun run typecheck` - passes
- ✅ `bun test` - passes (3 tests including GET confirm 404 verification)
- ✅ `bunx guren check` - passes all 16 checks
- ✅ `bunx guren check --arch` - passes architecture validation

The newsletter module is now self-contained and can be lifted into another application without any blog-specific dependencies.
